instruction: Open /home/user/Desktop/plate_100x60x12.step in FreeCAD 0.21.2. Open the part in FreeCAD from `/usr/bin/freecad`, then carry out the Path workbench edits when working on `plate_100x60x12.step`. Use the actual supplied solid: its source STEP bounds are X=-60..60 mm, Y=-40..40 mm, and Z=0..12 mm. Create one native Path/CAM Job with rectangular stock extended 2 mm on every X/Y side, 0 mm below, and 1 mm above the model. Set G54 at the stock top-face center. In this work coordinate system the stock top is Z=0 and the source plate top Z=12.000 mm is WCS Z=-1.000 mm. Create one active native Face operation that machines the complete stock top down to that plate top. Use T1, a 16 mm flat-bottom ToolBit used as a face mill, with spindle S6000 rpm and horizontal cutting feed F800 mm/min. Choose positive safe/clearance heights and a safe positive vertical feed; the facing pattern, angle, stepover, stepdown, and spindle direction are not otherwise fixed. Verify the generated toolpath, then post the Job with FreeCAD's native linuxcnc or grbl postprocessor. Save the editable native Job and its matching posted program at exactly /home/user/Desktop/task-1.FCStd and /home/user/Desktop/task-1.nc.
